places.name: Nelahozeves
places.country: Kingdom of Bohemia (Austrian Empire; today Czech Republic)
places.what: Born the eldest son of František and Anna Dvořák; his violin teacher Joseph Spitz taught him from 1847.

places.name: Zlonice
places.country: Kingdom of Bohemia (Austrian Empire; today Czech Republic)
places.what: Sent at thirteen to live with his uncle and learn German; a museum marks the stay.

places.name: Prague Organ School
places.country: Kingdom of Bohemia (Austrian Empire; today Czech Republic)
places.what: Studied singing, theory and organ, graduating second in his class; he played viola in orchestras from 1858.

places.name: Provisional Theatre, Prague
places.country: Kingdom of Bohemia (Austrian Empire; today Czech Republic)
places.what: Violist from 1862 in the orchestra that became the Provisional Theatre’s; Wagner conducted it in July 1863.

places.name: Prague
places.country: Kingdom of Bohemia (Austrian Empire; today Czech Republic)
places.what: The patriotic cantata The Heirs of the White Mountain was an “unqualified success” with the Hlahol choir of 300.
places.work: The Heirs of the White Mountain

places.name: Prague
places.country: Kingdom of Bohemia (Austrian Empire; today Czech Republic)
places.what: Won the Austrian State Prize; the jury included Hanslick and Brahms, who later recommended him to Simrock.

places.name: Royal Albert Hall, London
places.what: Stabat Mater was very well received under Joseph Barnby, sparking performances across Britain and the United States.

places.name: St James’s Hall, London
places.what: Conducted the premiere of his Seventh Symphony, written for the London Philharmonic Society.

places.name: Birmingham
places.what: Presented The Spectre’s Bride to 500 voices and 150 players; his Requiem premiered here in 1891.

places.name: Moscow and Saint Petersburg
places.what: Visited Russia at Tchaikovsky’s influence, conducting performances of his music in both cities.

places.name: Cambridge
places.what: Received an honorary degree from the University; he was also offered a Prague Conservatory professorship that year.

places.name: National Conservatory of Music, East 17th Street, New York
places.what: Director for three years; he lived at 327 East 17th Street; salary cuts and homesickness ended it.

places.name: Carnegie Hall, New York
places.what: The New York Philharmonic premiere of From the New World under Anton Seidl; each movement drew thunderous applause.

places.name: Spillville, Iowa
places.what: Summer holiday in a Czech-speaking community; wrote the American Quartet and the E♭ String Quintet.

places.name: Columbian Exposition, Chicago
places.what: Conducted a performance of his Eighth Symphony at the Exposition.

places.name: Vysoká
places.country: Kingdom of Bohemia (Austrian Empire; today Czech Republic)
places.what: Family cottage near the Kounic castle, whose fishpond inspired Rusalka; he returned here after the United States.

places.name: London
places.what: Premiere of the Cello Concerto by Leo Stern, written in New York; his last visit to London.

places.name: Vienna
places.what: Visited the dying Brahms, who had urged him to move to Vienna, and attended his funeral on 6 April.

places.name: Prague Conservatory
places.country: Kingdom of Bohemia (Austrian Empire; today Czech Republic)
places.what: Professor of composition from 1891 (again from November 1895); director from November 1901 until his death.

places.name: Prague
places.country: Kingdom of Bohemia (Austrian Empire; today Czech Republic)
places.what: Died of an undiagnosed cause after five weeks of illness and an influenza attack, aged sixty-two.

places.name: Vyšehrad Cemetery, Prague
places.country: Kingdom of Bohemia (Austrian Empire; today Czech Republic)
places.what: Funeral on 5 May; buried beneath a bust by Ladislav Šaloun.
